description.summary: monitor identity and MATE display semantics

protocol.description:
This protocol gives MATE's desktop components (display and appearance preferences, the file manager's desktop, the panel) what they need to know about monitors beyond wl_output and wlr-output-management: a stable monitor id, the monitor's EDID identity, the primary monitor, mirroring, the work area, and who draws the desktop background.
It extends two existing protocols instead of replacing them. Modes, positions, scale, transform and applying a layout stay in wlr-output-management-unstable-v1 (zwlr_output_manager_v1, version 4 or later); this protocol adds to its heads and configurations. For the file manager's desktop and the panel, which only see wl_output objects, it extends wl_output.
The protocol exposes information that can identify the user's hardware and lets the client change the primary monitor. A compositor should offer the global only to trusted MATE components, and never to clients in a sandbox.
Monitor ids. Every head and every enabled output has an id: a string of at most 255 bytes, made only of ASCII letters, digits and the characters "_", ".", "-", "@" and "+". Clients store settings under it, for example in GSettings paths, and must treat it as opaque. A compositor builds it as follows, so that ids agree across compositors and with clients that derive the id themselves when this protocol is missing:
1. Take the head's make and model (the strings wl_output.geometry and zwlr_output_head_v1.make and .model report), replace every byte that is not an ASCII letter or digit, "_", "." or "-" with "_", and join them with "-". Leave out a part that is empty, and the "-" with it. If both are empty, use "monitor". Call the result the base. 2. If no other connected head has the same base, the id is the base. 3. Otherwise, if the head has an EDID serial (the numeric serial written as 8 lowercase hexadecimal digits when it is not zero, else the serial number descriptor with the same character replacement) and no other connected head with the same base has the same serial, the id is the base, "-s" and the serial. 4. Otherwise the id is the base, "@" and the connector name (the zwlr_output_head_v1.name, with the same character replacement).
The id of a head is computed over the heads connected at the time. A monitor's id therefore only changes when a monitor with the same base is connected or disconnected, and never because a monitor moved. Rule 4 ids follow the connector.
Primary. Whenever at least one head is enabled, exactly one enabled head is primary. When the primary head is disabled or disconnected, the compositor chooses another one.
Mirroring. Enabled heads at the same position with the same logical size show the same picture: they mirror each other. The compositor reports which of them the picture is made for with mirror_of.
Layout. The compositor accepts a configuration in which enabled heads do not overlap, or overlap exactly as mirrors. It may refuse other overlaps, and gaps between heads, with zwlr_output_configuration_v1.failed; clients should close gaps before applying.
Versioning. This protocol follows the usual Wayland rules: a later version only adds requests, events and enum values, and a client must ignore enum and bitfield values it does not know.

interface.name: mate_output_manager_v1
interface.description: The global. After binding, the compositor sends the capabilities event before any other event.

entry.name: already_constructed
entry.summary: the wlr configuration already has a mate configuration

entry.name: already_used
entry.summary: the wlr configuration was already applied or tested

enum.name: capability
enum.description: Background drawing the compositor offers. When it offers wallpaper, it draws the desktop background on every output that no client covers with a desktop background of its own, following the org.mate.background settings: the shared ones, or an output's own org.mate.background.monitor settings at the path of its id when their use-shared key is false. A client such as a file manager desktop may then draw only its icons on a transparent surface. Without wallpaper, a client must not do that, or the desktop shows black.

entry.name: per_output_wallpaper
entry.summary: draws an output's own org.mate.background.monitor settings

entry.name: spanned_wallpaper
entry.summary: spans pictures over the outputs that share the settings

event.name: capabilities
event.description: Sent right after binding, and again whenever the capabilities change.

request.name: get_head

description.summary: MATE information for a wlr-output-management head

request.description: Creates a mate_output_head_v1 for the given head, which must belong to the same client. If the head has already finished, the new object sends finished at once.

request.name: get_output
request.description: Creates a mate_output_v1 for the given output. If the output's global has gone, the object sends nothing.

request.name: get_configuration

description.summary: MATE options for a wlr-output-management configuration

request.description: Creates a mate_output_configuration_v1 that adds options to the given configuration. It must be created before the configuration is applied or tested, and at most once per configuration.

request.name: stop
request.description: The compositor sends finished and no further events on this object. Objects created from it stay valid.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the compositor sends no more events

event.description: After this event the client should destroy the object.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Objects created from it stay valid.

interface.name: mate_output_head_v1
interface.description: Every event below belongs to a group that ends with done. The full state is sent after creation; later, only what changed is sent, followed by done.

event.name: id
event.description: See the protocol description for the rules.

event.name: edid_identity
event.description: The EDID's three-letter PNP vendor code, product code, numeric serial, and the serial number descriptor. A vendor and serial string that are unknown are empty; a product and serial that are unknown are 0. Sent once, before the first done.

event.name: edid
event.description: A read-only file descriptor the client may map, with the size of the EDID. Sent once, before the first done, and only when there is one.

event.name: display_name

description.summary: a name to show the user

event.description: A human-readable, possibly translated name, such as the EDID's monitor name, or the vendor and diagonal size.

description.summary: whether this is a built-in panel

event.name: primary

description.summary: whether this head is the primary monitor

event.description: Always 0 while the head is disabled.

event.name: mirror_of

description.summary: the head whose picture this one shows
end of a group of changes

event.name: finished
event.description: Sent when the zwlr_output_head_v1 finishes. The object then sends no more events, and the client should destroy it.

interface.name: mate_output_v1
interface.description: The same identity as mate_output_head_v1, plus what desktop clients need. Every event below belongs to a group that ends with done. The full state is sent after creation; later, only what changed is sent, followed by done.

entry.name: client
entry.summary: a client's desktop surface draws it

description.summary: a name to show the user
whether this is a built-in panel
whether this output is the primary monitor
the output whose picture this one shows

event.name: workarea
event.description: The part of the output where ordinary windows go, without the space panels and docks reserve, in output-relative logical coordinates (see xdg_output_v1.logical_size), with (0, 0) at the top-left corner. The whole output when nothing is reserved.

event.name: background_owner

description.summary: who draws this output's desktop background now

event.description: client while a client's desktop surface covers the output and draws its background; compositor while the compositor draws it, including under a client's transparent desktop surface; none otherwise.

description.summary: end of a group of changes

interface.name: mate_output_configuration_v1
interface.description: Options applied together with its zwlr_output_configuration_v1, all or nothing. Once that configuration has been applied, tested or destroyed, requests other than destroy raise already_used.

entry.name: invalid_head
entry.summary: the head belongs to another configuration

entry.name: already_used
entry.summary: the configuration was already applied, tested or destroyed

request.name: set_primary
request.description: Makes the head of this configuration_head primary when the configuration applies. The configuration_head must come from the same zwlr_output_configuration_v1. Without this request the compositor keeps the current primary while it stays enabled, and chooses one otherwise.

request.name: set_temporary
request.description: The configuration applies as usual but is not saved: it lasts until another configuration applies, a monitor is connected or disconnected, or the session ends. A client that asks the user whether to keep a layout applies it as temporary first, and applies it again without this request when the user keeps it.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroying it before the configuration is applied drops its options.
